boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Oregon rituals and recurring campus traditions, from orientation through commencement.

cards.title: Start with IntroDUCKtion
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Attend the university’s new-student orientation to register for classes, meet an advisor, and make your first connections as a Duck.
cards.short_summary: UO’s named entry-point tradition for incoming students.
cards.evidence_claim: UO identifies IntroDUCKtion as its new-student orientation and a first step into life as a Duck.
cards.access_notes: Registration and program details vary by incoming-student cohort.

cards.title: Join Week of Welcome
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Use the start-of-term welcome events to meet people and explore campus offerings, from crafts and therapy dogs to organized watch parties.
cards.short_summary: A recurring welcome-week ritual for new Ducks.
cards.evidence_claim: UO presents Week of Welcome as a tradition for students to settle in, connect, and explore campus activities.
cards.access_notes: Consult the university’s current Week of Welcome schedule for specific events.

cards.title: Come Home with the Flock
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon Homecoming · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Take part in the fall homecoming weekend through its pep rally, Run with the Duck, alumni gatherings, and athletic events.
cards.short_summary: UO’s homecoming tradition has brought the community together since 1914.
cards.evidence_claim: UO describes The Flock Comes Home as fall festivities that have brought students and alumni together since 1914.
cards.access_notes: Homecoming 2026 is scheduled for October 30–November 1; individual event access varies.

cards.title: Gather at the Mother’s Day Powwow
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Attend respectfully to experience the university’s annual powwow, which honors Native communities, mothers, and graduating seniors.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding UO powwow centered on Native community and recognition.
cards.evidence_claim: UO calls its Mother's Day Powwow the nation’s longest-running college powwow and describes its dances, ceremonies, and senior recognition.
cards.access_notes: Follow current event guidance and cultural-protocol information from organizers.

cards.title: Get Your Hands Dirty on University Day
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon campus · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Join the spring campus-care day by planting flowers or pulling weeds alongside the UO community and leave the grounds refreshed.
cards.short_summary: A spring service tradition that began in 1904.
cards.evidence_claim: UO states that University Day began in 1904 and brings the community together each spring to refresh campus grounds.
cards.access_notes: Participation opportunities are announced by UO for the current spring program.

cards.title: Wait for the Duck Reveal
cards.subtitle: Autzen Stadium · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: At commencement, celebrate graduating Ducks and watch for the traditional reveal of the person who has been inside the Duck costume.
cards.short_summary: UO pairs graduation ceremony with a mascot unmasking tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UO describes Commencement and Duck Reveal as a graduation tradition that includes finding out who was inside the Duck costume.
cards.access_notes: Commencement attendance and guest procedures are set for each graduating class.

cards.title: Stand Up for “Shout”
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon events and games · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: When “Shout” starts, join the crowd in the Duck anthem; the university links its campus history to Animal House, filmed at UO in 1978.
cards.short_summary: A crowd-singalong anthem tied directly to UO’s Animal House history.
cards.evidence_claim: UO identifies “Shout” as a Duck anthem and notes that Animal House was filmed on the UO campus in 1978.
cards.access_notes: Occurs as programmed at university and athletics events.

cards.title: Throw Your O
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon community · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Form an O with your hands to signal Oregon pride; it began as an Oregon Marching Band cue when Autzen was too loud for spoken direction.
cards.short_summary: A hand sign whose origin is rooted in the Oregon Marching Band.
cards.evidence_claim: OregonNews reports that band director Steven Paul created the O hand signal in the 1980s as a cue to play “Mighty Oregon.”
cards.source_title: O the Places You Will Go
cards.access_notes: A gesture used across UO community and athletics settings.

cards.title: Wear Green and Yellow on Duck Friday
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon community · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Wear UO green and yellow on Friday, then share your school-spirit look with #DuckFriday if you want to join the public ritual.
cards.short_summary: A weekly UO color-wearing tradition connecting Ducks on and off campus.
cards.evidence_claim: University Communications encourages Ducks to wear green and yellow on Fridays and calls the practice Duck Friday.
cards.access_notes: Participation is informal and does not require an event ticket.

cards.title: Learn “Mighty Oregon”
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon athletics and band tradition · Eugene, Oregon
cards.notes: Listen for the school fight song at Duck events and learn its refrain; UO says it was first performed on March 4, 1916.
cards.evidence_claim: OregonNews states that “Mighty Oregon” was first performed March 4, 1916 and continues as UO’s anthem.
cards.source_title: New 'Mighty Oregon' T-shirts raise money for marching band
cards.access_notes: Performed at applicable athletics and Oregon Marching Band appearances.
